name: Electronic
label: Factory Records
lede: New Order's singer and the Smiths' guitarist meant to put out anonymous white labels; instead they gave a collapsing Factory one of its last hit albums and kept going, on and off, for a decade.

eras.title: A side project that wouldn't stay anonymous
eras.text: Bernard Sumner and Johnny Marr first worked together on a Quando Quango record in 1984. By 1988 Sumner wanted somewhere to put the synth programming New Order didn't want, and Marr, free of The Smiths, was the person he called.

years.h: Marr plays on a Quando Quango track Sumner is producing
years.p: It's how the two met. The record was 'Atom Rock', issued by Factory that year.

years.cap: NME on Sumner and Marr's new project
years.h: Sumner starts a solo album and calls Marr instead
years.p: Frustrated that his New Order bandmates weren't keen on his synth programming, Sumner began a solo record, found working alone unfulfilling, and brought in Marr.
years.xp: The first plan, inspired by Italo house and acts like Technotronic, was a run of anonymous white-label twelve-inches on Factory. They dropped the anonymity, but the faceless name Electronic and a track called 'Lucky Bag' are left over from it.

years.h: Neil Tennant co-writes the first single and sings on it
years.p: [[Neil Tennant|8dac8c65-bcb3-4730-b82a-58727ea44e41]] of the [[Pet Shop Boys|be540c02-7898-4b79-9acc-c8122c7d9e83]] joined Sumner and Marr on 'Getting Away with It'. It went to No. 12 in the UK and sold about 350,000 copies.
years.xp: [[Anne Dudley|0b0bd0c0-3723-4715-87d7-9d57f0eb240f]] arranged the strings and ABC's David Palmer played drums. The UK video was directed by Chris Marker, the French filmmaker behind La Jetée.

years.cap: Melody Maker on Electronic's first shows, December 1990
years.h: Electronic opens for Depeche Mode in America
years.p: 'Getting Away with It' had reached No. 38 in the US that spring. The band toured as [[Depeche Mode|8538e728-ca0b-4321-b7e5-cff6565dd4c0]]'s support in August.

eras.title: Factory's last big record
eras.text: The album came out on Factory in May 1991 and went to No. 2. Eighteen months later Factory was in receivership, and Electronic's next release went elsewhere.

years.cap: NME advert for 'Get the Message', April 1991
years.h: 'Get the Message' goes to No. 1 on US Modern Rock
years.p: It reached No. 8 in the UK. 'Tighten Up' later got to No. 6 on the same US chart.

years.h: The debut album, made at Clear Studios and Marr's house
years.p: Recorded from December 1989 into early 1991 in Manchester, with Tennant and [[Chris Lowe|456163ba-4f9a-489a-bc14-ff7b3616dc9b]] on three tracks. No. 2 in the UK; more than a million sold worldwide.
years.xp:
Paul Lester in Melody Maker called it "one of the greatest albums ever made." Vox's Keith Cameron said it "simply achieves perfection."

NME and Melody Maker put it at No. 13 and No. 15 in their year-end polls. By 2000 it had sold 240,000 copies in the US.

years.h: 'Feel Every Beat' reaches No. 39
years.p: The third single from the debut album.

years.cap: Marr and Sumner on stage as Electronic, c. 1991
yt: 'Feel Every Beat', Cities in the Park 1991
years.h: Cities in the Park, then Paris, Glasgow and London
years.p: Electronic played the Cities in the Park festival in August and three shows in December. The Pet Shop Boys joined them for some of them.

years.h: With Tennant back, 'Disappointed' goes to No. 6
years.p: After Marr's work with [[The The|a7409219-a681-4072-adb2-5285106ce6f2]] and Sumner's with New Order, they regrouped with Tennant for their biggest UK hit.

eras.title: A Kraftwerk man commutes to Manchester
eras.text: The second album took the better part of two years. Karl Bartos, who'd left Kraftwerk, made the trip to Manchester throughout 1995 to write with them.

years.h: Karl Bartos joins the sessions
years.p: The ex-Kraftwerk percussionist co-wrote six of the album's 13 tracks and played keyboards. Ged Lynch drummed and [[Denise Johnson|105235af-71d6-4ea6-a141-f92d0ac6ae09]] sang backing vocals.

years.src: Wikipedia: Raise the Pressure · Wikipedia: Electronic
years.h: Jon Savage's punk history supplies the title
years.p: Raise the Pressure came out on Parlophone and reached No. 8. 'Forbidden City' and 'For You' both made the UK top 20.
years.xp:
Reviews were mixed, and some critics found the production overworked. Sumner and Marr agreed enough to spend far less time on the next one.

Sumner was taking Prozac in this period; he has said only one lyric on the album was written under its influence. The cover is a cherub painting by Johannes Handschin.

years.cap: Press feature on Electronic as a full-time band, July 1996
years.h: Top of the Pops and TFI Friday instead of a tour
years.p: Electronic played the singles on TV and went straight back into the studio.

years.src: Wikipedia: Electronic · Wikipedia: Raise the Pressure
years.h: 'Second Nature' closes the album's run at No. 35
years.p: The third single from Raise the Pressure.

eras.title: Four people, written fast
eras.text: After the long haul of the second album, the third was written and demoed quickly with a real band: Doves' bassist and Black Grape's drummer.

years.cap: Sumner and Marr in a Parlophone press photo
years.h: Jimi Goodwin of Doves and Ged Lynch of Black Grape join
years.p: [[Jimi Goodwin|75a0db19-d163-4981-83a9-cfb147619235]] played bass and Ged Lynch drums. [[Arthur Baker|6b6c5ce7-7a49-463a-ac9f-ba97c953a77e]] added scratches, harmonica and keyboards.

years.h: Twisted Tenderness reaches No. 9, and 'Vivid' No. 17
years.p: The third and last Electronic album, on Parlophone. Critics were warm to it; it didn't bring back the sales of the early 1990s.
years.xp: An uncleared Ice-T sample on early promo copies of 'Make It Happen' had to come off before release. 'King for a Day' was on the promos and international editions but ended up a B-side.

years.h: 'Late at Night' is withdrawn in the UK
years.p: The second single from Twisted Tenderness got two videos from director Jason Smith.

eras.title: Ended without an announcement
eras.text: A deluxe Twisted Tenderness in 2001 was the last release. Sumner went back to New Order; Marr went on to the Healers, Modest Mouse, The Cribs and solo records.

years.h: Neither of them ever announced a split
years.p: That's where Marr told Undercover the band had got to in 2003. He said he was happy with how it ended.

years.h: Sumner and Marr play with Doves at Manchester v Cancer
years.p: The two of them on one stage again, at the charity concert.

years.h: EMI puts out Get the Message: The Best of Electronic
years.p: It charted at No. 194.

years.cap: Bernard Sumner on stage at Jodrell Bank, July 2013
years.h: Sumner walks on at Jodrell Bank to sing 'Getting Away with It'
years.p: Marr was supporting New Order at the observatory. Sumner joined his set for Electronic's first single.
